name: Door
overview: Scripture reveals the significance of doors both physically and figuratively, as seen in the detailed descriptions of temple doors made of olive and fir trees, adorned with carvings of cherubim, flowers, and overlaid with gold (1 Kings 6:31-34). The doors and their posts served practical and symbolic purposes, such as the paschal lamb's blood sprinkled on the doorposts to protect God's people (Exodus 12:22) and the law written upon doorposts and gates as a reminder of God's commands (Deuteronomy 11:20). These passages highlight doors as points of transition and protection, embodying both divine presence and opportunity.
